item.title: The Machinery of Repair is Subject to the Same Damage it Seeks to Remove
item.description: A mouse or a human is a self-repairing system, up to a point. item.title: Better Glymphatic System Function Correlates with Lower Mortality Risk
item.description: The brain depends upon a flow of cerebrospinal fluid to carry away metabolic waste. This fluid is created in the choroid plexus, flows through the spaces of the brain, and then drains into the body via the glymphatic system. This drainage is most active during sleep. item.title: Icariin Enhances Mitophagy in the Aging Brain, Reducing Inflammation
item.description: Icariin is a flavonoid plant extract that has been studied in a number of contexts in recent years. Supplementation with icariin has been shown to improve the aged gut microbiome and slow a number of aspects of aging in mice. item.title: ZNF865 Regulates Cellular Senescence in Intervertebral Disc Tissues
item.description: Cellular senescence is strongly implicated in the onset and progression of degenerative disc disease, the atrophy and dysfunction of intervertebral discs in the spine. It is a prevalent cause of pain and loss of function in older people. Here, researchers explore the role of ZNF865 in regulating the senescent state in multiple cell types. item.title: Elevated Bile Salt Hydrolase Activity in the Gut Microbiome May Slow Aging
item.description: It is by now well established that the composition of the gut microbiome influences the pace of aging. item.title: Reviewing Efforts to Bring Klotho Therapies to the Clinic
item.description: Klotho is one of the more compelling longevity-associated genes; it is well demonstrated in animal models that reduced levels of klotho reduce life span, while increased levels increase life span.
